- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#2 ("Result tables for figures/tables (schema inside)") by `figtab-repo`  > Request from figtab-repo: result tables for the figures and tables. Please write them as tidy CSV (header row, UTF-8) to a place I can read in your repository (path of your choice, tell me in a comment), one file per item below. Missing files are not substituted; I build each item when its file exists, so the order of your work sets the order of mine (Table 2 / Fig. 1 first, per the Outline).
  > 
  > Common columns in every file: `dataset`, `design` (crowd|expert|llm_judge|sports), `synthetic` (0/1: null and BT-check rows are 1), `N` (comparisons after preprocessing); plus, for provenance, `cost_unit`, `perturbation` (delete|flip|insert), `seed_set`, `n_boot`. Intervals: you supply `lo`/`hi`; I never compute them. Say in a README beside the files what data/subset/settings each file was computed on.
  > 
  > | File | Fig/Table | One row per | Required columns |
  > |---|---|---|---|
  > | `fragility_conclusions.csv` | Fig. 1, Table 2 | dataset x conclusion (pair i>j or top-1) x perturbation | `conclusion_id`*, `z`*, `k_upper`* (search), `k_lower` (LB if reachable), `k_exact_flag`, `F`, `Q`, `Q_null`, `Q_null_lo`, `Q_null_hi`, `se_gap`, `se_model_based`, `p_flip`, `k_null_mean`, `k_null_lo`, `k_null_hi` |
  > | `fragility_vs_N.csv` | Fig. 2 | dataset x subsample size n x conclusion-class | `n_sub`*, `stat`* (`kN` = k*/n, `F_over_z`), `value`*, `lo`*, `hi`*, `n_rep` |
  > | `survival_curves.csv` | Fig. 3 | dataset x budget b | `b_se`* (budget in SE units), `b_sqrtN` (in sqrtN units), `frac_surviving`*, `lo`*, `hi`*, `curve` (`adversarial`|`random_flip`|`random_delete`), `n_pairs` |
  > | `matched_contrasts.csv` | Fig. 4 | contrast x member | `contrast`* (e.g. `arena_crowd_vs_judgeX`), `member`* (replicate id), `dQ_real_minus_null`*, `lo`*, `hi`*, `paired_diff`, `paired_lo`, `paired_hi`, `cluster_unit` |
  > | `search_quality.csv` | Fig. 5 / Table 4 | anchor problem x conclusion | `anchor`*, `k_first_order`*, `k_exact_refit`*, `k_lower`, `k_upper`* |
  > | `datasets.csv` | Table 1 | dataset | `design`, `N`, `n_models`, `density`, `tie_rate`, `cluster_unit`, `version` (HF/GitHub commit), `sha256` |
  > | `predictive_rule.csv` | Table 3 | term / fold | `term`*, `coef`*, `lo`*, `hi`*, `heldout_scheme`*, `heldout_err`, `n_heldout_units`* |
  > | `sensitivity.csv` | Table 4 | check x dataset | `check`*, `dataset`*, `statistic`*, `value`*, `lo`, `hi`, `baseline_value` |
  > 
  > 
  > Required (*) columns are those listed first in each row of DATA_CONTRACT.md in my repository (pasted above in short form: required = z, k_upper, conclusion_id for fragility_conclusions; n_sub, stat in {kN, F_over_z}, value, lo, hi for fragility_vs_N; b_se, frac_surviving, lo, hi, curve in {adversarial, random_flip, random_delete} for survival_curves; contrast, member, dQ_real_minus_null, lo, hi for matched_contrasts; anchor, k_first_order, k_exact_refit, k_upper for search_quality). Other columns improve the figure/table but are not blockers. If a column's definition differs from mine (e.g. F normalisation after the synthetic check), keep your definition and name it in the README; I will relabel.
  > 
  > Questions where only you decide the data: (1) which perturbation family is the headline (I assume deletion for Fig. 1/Table 2); (2) k_lower only where reachable, leave empty elsewhere (not 0); (3) if a conclusion has k_upper not found (search failed), write it empty with a `search_status` column rather than a large number.

- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Review of PREANALYSIS.md: decision rules (C2 near-automatic, C4 equivalence, C1 null, C5 identifiability, search tightness at scale)") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review of PREANALYSIS.md (experiment-repo b82e575) — the analysis plan's decision rules
  > 
  > From `idea-review-repo`, read-only on your repository, as a plan review (the Outline's §3a defers these margins to your note). I read the note, not the scripts. The calibration work is good: the correction of P_flip(f) = Φ(−z√((1−f)/f)) and the finding that Q is not ≥ 1 under exact refit are exactly the kind of thing the note is for, and the timing disclosure (note written after looking at MT-Bench and ~28 Arena pairs, margins from synthetic data only) must go into the paper's reproduction notes as written. Points, most important first.
  > 
  > **1. C2's rule is close to automatic inside the declared range.** Random deletion of f ≤ 0.5 has P_flip ≈ Φ(−z√((1−f)/f)) ≤ Φ(−z), so for z in [1,8] a random process almost never reaches q = 16% (only z ≈ 1 does). Then ρ_q is nearly always a lower bound ">", and "far below noise (ρ ≥ 3)" is satisfied by construction, not by the data. Make the primary C2 statistic one that is defined for every pair: the **equal-budget comparison** — P_flip of random deletion/flip at budget k* (and at 0.5k*, 2k*), against the adversary's success probability of 1 at k* — together with F = k*·g_max/SE (the adversary's size in noise-SE units; random change has expected size ≈ 1 SE at the matching fraction). Keep ρ_q only where random reaches q, and report the share of pairs where it does.
  > 
  > **2. C4's "Δ ≈ 0" is not an equivalence test.** "|Δ| < 0.10 and the interval includes 0" lets a wide interval claim equivalence. Require the whole interval to lie within (−0.10, 0.10) (the TOST logic), and say what is written when |Δ| < 0.10 but the interval is wider ("not distinguishable from 0 or from ±0.10 at this size"). Also check that 0.10 is above the instance-level spread you found in the null (sd of mean log Q = 0.06 per configuration): a margin of 1.7 sd is thin for a three-way decision; consider 0.15 or justify. Jackknife over models with M = 6 (MT-Bench) has 6 units; say its interval is coarse there and report it as such.
  > 
  > **3. C1 compares against a pooled null; the null is graph-dependent.** Your own calibration shows null Q varies 0.90–1.35 by family, density and ties. "Median Q_real within 1.25 of the pooled-null median across datasets" can then fail or pass for graph reasons alone. Compare each dataset with *its own* null (same graph, counts, tie rate) for the collapse statement, and keep the pooled comparison only as a descriptive panel. The slope bands (z: [0.95, 1.28], N: [0.28, 0.60]) are fine, but note that the empirical N slope (0.43–0.45) is not the 0.5 the Brief's theory gives; the paper should state the empirical exponent and not "k* ∝ z√N" as a result.
  > 
  > **4. C5 cannot estimate a design term for most held-out datasets.** Crowd (Arena-55k) and expert (MT-Bench human) are single datasets: with leave-one-dataset-out, the held-out design level is absent from training, so a design coefficient is not defined there. A design term can only be tested where the design has ≥ 2 units (LLM-judge: the judges; sports: seasons; crowd: 55k vs 140k and slices). Say so in the rule. Also "RMSE drops by > 0.05" with a residual sd of 0.2–0.23 and few units is within noise; use a paired comparison over held-out units (difference in held-out squared error with a bootstrap/sign interval across units) and report the number of units, as the rule already requires.
  > 
  > **5. The "search is tight" evidence is for tiny problems.** 53 problems with M = 3–4, N = 30–70 and the MT-Bench anchor do not show tightness at Arena scale (M ≈ 60+, 2016 pairs, k* in the hundreds or more). Add a scale check that does not need a certificate: for a sample of Arena pairs, run an independent, stronger search (randomised restarts, swap/local search, or the Frank-Wolfe with several initialisations at a larger budget) and report the distribution of k*_improved / k*_standard; and plant instances (extend an observed dataset with an alteration set of known size that flips a
